title: Highest-Protein Meats: Ranking Per 100 Grams

seo.title: Highest-Protein Meats per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Rank chicken, turkey, beef and pork by protein per 100 grams and learn why cut, fat and cooking water matter more than species labels.
seo.search_intent: Rank common meats by protein density.

excerpt: Cooked chicken and turkey breast sit near 30 grams of protein per 100 grams, but lean beef and pork are close behind. Cut and cooking loss matter more than broad species stereotypes.
content_html:
The highest-protein meat depends on the cut and whether you measure it raw or cooked. Once lean meats are cooked, several cluster between roughly 27 and 31 grams per 100 grams.

Representative cooked ranking

CutApprox. protein/100 g
Skinless chicken breast31 g
Skinless turkey breast29–30 g
Lean beef cuts27–30 g
Pork loin/tenderloin27–29 g
Skinless chicken thigh25–27 g
Lean cooked ground meat25–28 g

Chicken breast

Cooked skinless breast is a benchmark because it combines about 31 g protein per 100 g with little fat. A 150 g serving can approach 46 g.

Turkey breast

Turkey breast is nutritionally very close. A one- or two-gram difference per 100 g is rarely meaningful enough to choose one bird over the other.

Lean beef

Many trimmed beef cuts provide nearly as much protein while offering relatively rich amounts of heme iron, zinc and B12. Marbling raises fat and calories more than protein.

Lean pork

Pork tenderloin and loin challenge the idea that pork is inherently fatty. Lean preparations can rival beef and poultry for protein density.

Why cooked values look higher

Raw chicken breast may contain only 22–23 g per 100 g. Cooking removes water, so the same protein becomes concentrated into a lighter piece of meat. Protein did not appear in the oven.

Fresh meat versus deli meat

Turkey breast deli slices may contain added water, sodium and binders. If protein density matters, compare the Nutrition Facts panel rather than assuming a product labeled “turkey” matches roasted turkey breast.

Frequently asked questions

What meat has the most protein?

Cooked skinless chicken breast is commonly near the top at about 31 g per 100 g, with turkey and lean beef or pork close behind.

Does raw meat contain less protein?

Per 100 g it usually appears lower because raw meat contains more water.

Is pork a high-protein food?

Yes. Lean loin and tenderloin are protein-dense and can be relatively low in fat.

faq.question: Which meat has the most protein per 100 g?
faq.answer: Cooked skinless chicken breast commonly sits near 31 g, with turkey and lean beef or pork close behind.

faq.question: Why does cooked meat look higher in protein?
faq.answer: Water is lost during cooking, concentrating protein per unit of weight.

faq.question: Is lean pork high in protein?
faq.answer: Yes. Tenderloin and loin can provide about 27–29 g per 100 g cooked.
